subtopics.name: Integration by Parts and Special Integrals

questions.stem: The integral $\int \frac{\left(x^2 - 1\right) dx}{\left(x^4 + 3x^2 + 1\right) \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{x^2 + 1}{x}\right)}$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Divide numerator and denominator by $x^2$:
$I = \int \frac{(1 - 1/x^2) dx}{(x^2 + 3 + 1/x^2) \tan^{-1}(x + 1/x)} = \int \frac{(1 - 1/x^2) dx}{((x + 1/x)^2 + 1) \tan^{-1}(x + 1/x)}$.
Let $t = \tan^{-1}(x + 1/x)$. Then $dt = \frac{1}{1 + (x+1/x)^2} \cdot (1 - 1/x^2) dx$.
The integral becomes $\int \frac{dt}{t} = \ln|t| + C = \ln\left| \tan^{-1}\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right) \right| + C$.

questions.stem: If $\int e^{2x} \left( \frac{1 - \sin 2x}{1 + \cos 2x} \right) dx = e^{2x} f(x) + C$, then $f(x)$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Let $I = \int e^{2x} \left( \frac{1 - 2\sin x \cos x}{2\cos^2 x} \right) dx = \int e^{2x} \left( \frac{1}{2}\sec^2 x - \tan x \right) dx$.
Let $2x = t \implies dx = dt/2$.
$I = \frac{1}{2} \int e^t \left( \frac{1}{2}\sec^2(t/2) - \tan(t/2) \right) dt = -\frac{1}{2} \int e^t \left( \tan(t/2) - \frac{1}{2}\sec^2(t/2) \right) dt$.
Since $\frac{d}{dt}\tan(t/2) = \frac{1}{2}\sec^2(t/2)$, this is of the form $-\frac{1}{2} e^t \tan(t/2) + C = -\frac{1}{2} e^{2x} \tan x + C$.
Hence $f(x) = -\frac{1}{2}\tan x$.
